title: Why India’s Cockroach Movement Might Not Collapse Like the Others
gist: After Indian Supreme Court Justice Surya Kant compared unemployed youth and activists to cockroaches and parasites in May, millions of young Indians adopted 'Main Bhi Cockroach' and launched a political party; the author argues the standard top-down reading (Modi misreading the environment) misses the peer-to-peer digital mechanics that also drove Gen Z uprisings in Nepal, Bangladesh, Kenya and Madagascar.

insights.claim: Indian Supreme Court Justice Surya Kant's May comparison of certain unemployed youth and activists to cockroaches and parasites was converted within days into the rallying cry 'Main Bhi Cockroach,' adopted by millions and used to launch a political party.
insights.speaker: Marvin Starominski-Uehara
insights.so_what: A new youth-unemployment party forming inside India's electoral system is a live domestic political risk to policy continuity - watch whether it contests state polls.
insights.quote: Millions of young Indians declared “Main Bhi Cockroach” (‘I too am a cockroach’), turned the insult into memes, and launched a political party in the same breath.

insights.claim: The movement's grievance base is India's marginalized and unemployed youth, with protest demands centered on alleged examination irregularities and education reforms.
insights.speaker: Marvin Starominski-Uehara
insights.so_what: Youth unemployment and exam-integrity failures are the mobilizing wedge - a signal that labor-market data, not identity politics, is the emerging Indian political fault line.

insights.claim: The author explicitly rejects the classic top-down framing that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government simply misread the political environment, arguing it overlooks emerging leadership theories, peer-to-peer digital communication mechanics, and global trends already underway.
insights.speaker: Marvin Starominski-Uehara
insights.so_what: If the movement is structurally digital rather than a reaction to one government error, it is less likely to be defused by conciliatory messaging from Delhi.
